feeding a high cal% diet of partially hydrogenated fish fat induced morphological and functional changes at the mitochondrial and the peroxisome level.

essential fatty acid deficiency induced by feeding a high cal% fish oil diet resulted in megamitochondrial proliferation in rat liver, whereas peroxosomal proliferation was induced by factors other than essential fatty acid deficiency.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of essential fatty acid (EFA) deficiency on mitochondria, and peroxisome proliferation in rat hepatocytes.
the effect of essential fatty acid deficient diet on mitochondrial and peroxisosomal function and structure of hepatocytes.
the effect of dietary factors on the morphology and the biochemistry of rat liver mitochondria and per-oxisomes.

the effects of essential fatty acid-deficiency on mitochondrial structure and function are fully prevented by adding sufficient linoleic acid, whereas perox isomal proliferation is not prevented by linoleic acid supplementation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the essential fatty acid deficiency is a key factor in the development of mitochondrial changes, whereas the peroxisomes are affected by other factors.
the partially hydrogenated fat diet induced an essential fatty acid deficient state and a peroxisomal proliferating state in the rat hepatocyte.
the essential fatty acid deficiency induced by partially hydrogenated vegetable oils is a major factor in the development of mitochondrial and peroxosomal alterations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of partially hydrogenated fish oils should be discouraged, as they induce essential fatty acid deficiency in rats and may do so in humans.
